brief:
Today, 17 November, is a rest day. You have now trained eight days in a row, 9 to 16 November, through the two days I set as rest (15 and 16 November). Nothing is broken: every lift on Pull A on 16 November held or went up. But the lighter week does not start until 25 November, and a ninth straight day is not how to get there. Rest today; Legs A is tomorrow, 18 November.

If you train today anyway, the Legs A card already has my numbers on it. The last two rest-day reviews put no numbers on the card and you trained on the app's own numbers both times. That is why the wide pulldown on 16 November opened at 112.5 and 127.5 when I wanted 135 on every set. From today the card carries the review's numbers on a rest day too.

Pull A on 16 November, what it showed: deadlift 215, 235, 245, 250 for 5, 10 lb up on every set. Wide pulldown top set 135 for 8, up from 127.5. Seated row 112.5 for 10 on all four, up from 105. Dumbbell curl 35 for 8 on all three, up from 30. Hammer curl 42.5 for 11, 12, 12, one rep short of the next weight. Face pulls 32.5 for 12, 12, three reps under 13 November; that was the last lift of an eighth straight day and the weight holds. The app now marks the seated row "stalled". It is not: that label is comparing you with 115 at the Singapore and Vancouver gyms. Same wrong label as the chest press, and it needs a change to the app's code, which this review is not allowed to make.

Legs A numbers (tomorrow, or today if you train): leg press 210 for 8 on all three. Calf press second, 300 for 13 on all three, no lighter first sets. Split squat 25 in each hand for 8, 8. Leg curl 157.5 for 11 on all three. Leg extension 157.5 for 12, 12. Adductor 97.5 for 12, 12 and abductor 127.5 for 12, 12 (nearest weight above last time if the machine does not have those). Ab machine 65 for 12 on all three.

No program change today (still version 13). Every lift logged at this gym in the last eight days went up or held its weight, except that face pulls lost three reps a set at the same weight on 16 November. So there is no lift to rotate and no muscle to cut or raise before the lighter week. If you rest today the days run: Legs A 18 November, Push B 19, Pull B 20, Legs B 21, Push A 22, Pull A 23, rest 24, lighter week from 25 November. If you train today, each of those moves one day earlier.

Still open: if calf press is skipped again on the next Legs A, which calf machine does the New York gym have? If the shrug's fourth set is missing again on the next Pull B, the card drops to three sets. Your 16 November log is stamped Meso 3, week 8; if the phase at the top of the app is locked, the 25 November lighter week will not start by itself, and "Automatic (by date)" clears the lock. No bodyweight has been logged since 23 August, so a morning weigh-in would help.

One question I am still leaving open: you asked on 2 and 10 November whether the set counts are supported. Front delts, rear delts, upper back, biceps, triceps and forearms sit inside their ranges if only direct sets count, but above them if every compound lift's helper work is counted. Until the program is rebuilt on 9 December, those six get more total work than the ranges say; that rebuild settles the count on one rule for every muscle.

Today: rest. An easy 20 to 30 minute walk or bike ride is fine. Eat and sleep like it is a training day.

block.why: Today, 17 November, is a rest day. The 16 November review set rest for 16 November and you trained Pull A, as you trained Push A on 15 November when that was set as rest, so 9 to 16 November is eight sessions in a row, past the six-session limit. It is day 21 of the block restarted on 28 October at the New York gym, the last day of week 3 of 4; the build runs to 24 November, the lighter (deload) week is 25 November to 1 December, assessment 2 to 8 December, prep from 9 December, and the show is 104 days away. The block is doing what a build block should: Pull A on 16 November was all done (19 of 19 sets) and five of six lifts went up on the 10 November visit: deadlift 250 for 5 on the top set, wide pulldown 135 for 8, seated row 112.5 for 10 on all four, dumbbell curl 35 for 8 on all three, hammer curl 42.5 for 11, 12, 12. Face pulls held their weight with fewer reps. No program change today: every lift logged at this gym since 9 November went up or held its weight (face pulls held the weight and lost three reps a set on 16 November), no muscle is short of its range with stalled lifts, and the deload and the December assessment need like-for-like numbers. One thing does change in how this review is delivered: the last two rest-day reviews put no numbers on the card and you trained both days on the app's own numbers, so today's Legs A card carries the review's numbers even though the call is rest. Two watches keep their conditions: calf press on the next Legs A, the shrug's fourth set on the next Pull B. If you rest today the days run Legs A 18 November, Push B 19, Pull B 20, Legs B 21, Push A 22, Pull A 23, rest 24 November; if you train today each moves one day earlier. At 25 November the deload cuts sets and holds weights at or a little under the last working weight. The exercise list is rebuilt for prep on 9 December, and that rebuild settles the set-count question you have asked about since 2 November on one counting rule. Sessions stay 19, 19, 20, 20, 21, 20 sets.

findings.finding: Three muscle explanations did not match the program's muscle map: hamstrings counted the deadlift as half credit (it is a main hamstring lift; 13 direct plus 1 from the split squat makes 14); forearms said three direct sets with help from rows and the deadlift (it is six direct, hammer curl and reverse curl, with half credit from the dumbbell curl, shrug and RDL); traps said half credit from rows (it is the deadlift and face pulls). The planned and averaged numbers were right; the breakdowns were wrong.
findings.why: All three breakdowns rewritten from the catalogue and now add up to the planned figure.

findings.finding: The reason for changing nothing said every lift "went up or held", but face pulls went from 32.5 for 15, 15 on 13 November to 32.5 for 12, 12 on 16 November, which the packet's own flag calls a drop.
findings.why: Brief and block now say every lift went up or held its weight, and that face pulls lost three reps a set at the same weight.

findings.finding: The shrug verdict said the missing fourth set was "not on the longest nights"; it was missing on the shortest New York Pull B (29 October, 46 minutes) and on the longest (13 November, 53 minutes).
findings.why: The clause is replaced with the two nights and their lengths.

findings.finding: The split squat card and brief hedged "if the rack has no 25s", though the log shows 25 lb dumbbells at this gym (incline curl 25 for 10 on 29 October).
findings.why: The fallback is removed from the card, the brief and the verdict; the verdict cites the 29 October set.

findings.finding: The reviewer could not confirm that the 16 November deadlift was "exactly the card": the app's card was not reproduced.
findings.why: The verdict now says only what is on record: these were the weights the 16 November review gave.

findings.finding: Carried from 16 November: the app labels lifts "stalled" by comparing with other gyms; today the seated row joined the chest press, high-to-low crossover, straight-arm pulldown and reverse curl.
findings.why: The stall check is app code, which this review may not edit. The review states the true trend for each of the five lifts.
findings.consequence: Until the code is fixed, the app shows "stalled" on five lifts that each went up at the New York gym; ignore that label on them.

findings.finding: Carried from 16 November: muscles are judged inside range on direct sets while six of them (front delts, rear delts, upper back, biceps, triceps, forearms) are above their ceilings once helper work is counted.
findings.why: The counting rule is not changed mid-block; it is settled for every muscle at the 9 December rebuild. Each muscle verdict prints both counts.
findings.consequence: Until 9 December those six muscles get more total work than their ranges say once helper work is counted.
